sounds.name: First Squelch
sounds.ref: In the style of Phuture — "Acid Tracks"
sounds.blurb: The classic acid line: a buzzy sawtooth that squelches on every note and shrieks on the accents.
sounds.how: One sawtooth goes through a resonant low-pass filter. The envelope flicks the filter open on each note and DECAY closes it again, and RESONANCE turns that movement into a squelch. Accented steps open the filter further and play louder, and slid steps glide into the next note.

steps.title: A sawtooth, filter half open
steps.why:
Everything starts with one oscillator. The sawtooth carries every harmonic, so it gives the filter the most to work on.
- WAVEFORM sawtooth: bright and buzzy.
- CUT OFF FREQ 3.5: fairly low, so between notes the sound is dark.
- Listen for: play the riff. It is a dull, plodding bass for now.

steps.title: Turn up the resonance
steps.why:
RESONANCE boosts the frequencies at the cutoff point. On the TB-303 that is the squelch.
- RESONANCE 8: a strong, vocal peak that follows the filter as it moves.
- Listen for: each note now has a rubbery "yow". Turn RESONANCE back to 2 and the line goes plain again.

steps.title: Let the envelope open it
steps.why:
ENV MOD sets how far each note opens the filter before DECAY closes it. With high resonance that sweep is the acid sound.
- ENV MOD 6: a big sweep on every note.
- DECAY 3.5 (about 450 ms): each note closes fairly quickly, so the line stays tight.
- Listen for: the squelch gets wider. Turn DECAY up and the notes smear into long "wows".

steps.title: Accents
steps.why:
The riff has accented steps. ACCENT sets how much they stand out: louder, quicker to close, and with an extra sweep of the filter that grows with RESONANCE.
- ACCENT 7: the accented notes jump out with a sharp shriek.
- Listen for: the pattern of loud and quiet notes. Turn ACCENT to 0 and the line goes flat.

context.filter.res: The squelch. Most acid lines live between 7 and 10.
context.filter.cutoff: Sweep this slowly while the riff plays. That slow sweep is how acid tracks build.
context.filter.envMod: How far each note opens. Low values keep the line dark and the accents stand out more.
context.env.decay: How long each note takes to close. Short is tight and plucky; long smears the notes into each other.
context.amp.accent: How hard the accented steps hit.

tweaks.try: Sweep slowly from 2 to 8 while the riff plays
tweaks.hear: The line opens from a muffled thud into a screaming squelch.
Each note becomes a long, wet "wow".
A hollower, rounder line with the same squelch.

sounds.name: Round Pop Bass
sounds.ref: In the style of 1980s synth pop bass lines
sounds.blurb: A soft, rounded bass, the job the TB-303 was sold for.
sounds.how: The square wave and a mostly closed filter with little resonance give a round, woody bass. A modest ENV MOD gives each note a soft thump at the front. Without heavy resonance the filter just shapes the tone.

steps.title: Square wave
steps.why:
The square wave has only odd harmonics, which makes it hollow and round compared with the sawtooth.
- WAVEFORM square.
- Listen for: play a few low notes. It sounds woody rather than buzzy.

steps.title: A dark, gentle filter
steps.why:
The filter is kept low with little resonance, so it only rounds the tone.
- CUT OFF FREQ 3, RESONANCE 1: soft and round.
- ENV MOD 3, DECAY 3: a small thump at the start of each note.
- Listen for: a bass that sits under a song instead of shouting over it.

steps.title: Light accents
steps.why:
This riff has no accented steps, so ACCENT only matters if you play with the ACCENT button lit.
- ACCENT 3: a little extra punch when accents are used.

context.filter.cutoff: Keeps the bass round. Above about 5 it starts to buzz.
context.filter.res: Kept low so the bass does not squelch.
context.osc.wave: The square is what makes it round. The sawtooth is brighter.

tweaks.hear: The bass starts to talk, a step towards acid.
The thump goes and the notes are flat and smooth.

sounds.name: Sliding Acid Line
sounds.ref: In the style of Hardfloor — "Acperience 1"
sounds.blurb: A fast, winding line full of slides, with a long decay and high resonance.
sounds.how: Slides glide the pitch into the next step and do not start the envelope again, so a run of slid notes is one long squelch that bends through the pitches. A longer DECAY and high RESONANCE make that squelch wet and vocal, and accents punctuate it.

steps.title: Sawtooth and a low filter
steps.why:
The usual acid start: a sawtooth through a filter that is mostly closed.
- WAVEFORM sawtooth, CUT OFF FREQ 3.
- Listen for: the riff is dull for now.

steps.title: High resonance, long decay
steps.why:
High resonance makes the filter sing, and a long DECAY lets that song carry through the slides.
- RESONANCE 9, ENV MOD 5.
- DECAY 6 (about 800 ms): the filter is still closing when the next note slides in.
- Listen for: the slid notes run together into one bending wail.

steps.title: Strong accents
steps.why:
Accents cut through the long notes with a short, loud, bright hit.
- ACCENT 8.
- Listen for: the accented notes snap even though the rest are smeared.

context.env.decay: Long here, so slides carry the squelch from one pitch to the next.
context.filter.res: Near the top, so the line sings.
context.amp.accent: The accents cut through the long notes.

tweaks.try: Light SLIDE and play the keyboard
tweaks.hear: Every note you play now glides from the last.
The line becomes tight and stabbing, and the slides stand out more.

sounds.name: Dark Rumble
sounds.ref: In the style of minimal acid techno
sounds.blurb: A low, nearly closed line where only the accents open up.
sounds.how: With the cutoff and ENV MOD low, ordinary notes stay dark and muffled. ACCENT is turned right up with high resonance, so only the accented steps break out with a bright yelp. The contrast is the groove.

steps.title: Closed filter
steps.why:
The filter starts almost shut, so ordinary notes are just a low thud.
- CUT OFF FREQ 2, ENV MOD 1.5, DECAY 3.
- Listen for: a dark, muted pulse.

steps.title: Resonance for the accents
steps.why:
RESONANCE also sets how far an accent pushes the filter. Raising it makes the accented notes jump much more than the rest.
- RESONANCE 8.
- Listen for: the accented steps start to poke out.

steps.title: Accent right up
steps.why:
ACCENT at full makes the accented steps much louder and brighter.
- ACCENT 10.
- Listen for: a dark line punctuated by sharp yelps.

context.amp.accent: Does most of the work here. Turn it down and the line goes flat.
context.filter.res: Sets how far each accent opens the filter.
context.filter.cutoff: Kept low so only the accents are bright.

tweaks.hear: The accents get louder but no longer yelp.
Every note opens and the accents stop standing out.

sounds.name: Jacking House Line
sounds.ref: In the style of Armando — "Land of Confusion"
sounds.blurb: A raw Chicago acid house line where held notes open and close slowly under heavy resonance.
sounds.how: A sawtooth goes through the filter with RESONANCE near the top and ENV MOD high, so every note is a wide sweep. DECAY is set longer than usual, and the riff ties some notes over two steps, so you hear the filter closing all the way down. ENV MOD also pulls the resting cutoff down a little, which keeps the gaps between sweeps dark.

steps.title: Sawtooth, filter low
steps.why:
Start from the plain acid voice: one sawtooth and a filter that is mostly closed.
- WAVEFORM sawtooth: every harmonic, so the filter has plenty to work on.
- CUT OFF FREQ 3 (about 450 Hz): dark between notes.
- Listen for: a dull, thudding line. The tied notes on the first and ninth steps last twice as long as the rest.

steps.title: Big sweep, slow close
steps.why:
High RESONANCE and ENV MOD make each note a wide "yow", and a longer DECAY slows the close so you can follow it.
- RESONANCE 9: a strong peak that rides the sweep.
- ENV MOD 7: each note opens the filter a long way. It also lowers the resting cutoff a little, so the line is darker between notes.
- DECAY 5 (about 630 ms): the filter is still closing when the next note starts.
- Listen for: the tied notes. They open bright and you can hear them close right down before the next note.

steps.title: Moderate accents
steps.why:
With ENV MOD this high, every note is already loud and bright, so ACCENT is set in the middle.
- ACCENT 5: the two accented steps stand out without taking over.
- Listen for: the jump to the upper C on step 4 is louder and snaps shut quickly. Accented notes close the filter in 0.2 s whatever DECAY says.

context.filter.envMod: Set high, so every note sweeps. It also pulls the resting cutoff down a little; turn it to 2 and the line is brighter between notes but flat.
context.env.decay: Long enough to hear each sweep close. Below 3 the notes become short blips; above 7 they run into each other.
context.filter.res: Near the top for the squelch. Below about 6 the sweeps lose their vocal sound.
context.filter.cutoff: The resting point. Raise it slowly over a few bars to build the track.
context.amp.accent: Middle setting, because the ordinary notes are already loud.

tweaks.try: Turn slowly from 3 to 6 over several bars
tweaks.hear: The line opens from a thud into a bright, buzzing squelch.
The tied notes no longer sweep; they click open and stay dark.

sounds.name: Rising Acid
sounds.ref: In the style of Josh Wink — "Higher State of Consciousness"
sounds.blurb: A fast, unbroken run of sixteenth notes at full resonance, built to be opened up slowly by hand.
sounds.how: Every step plays, so the filter is struck sixteen times a bar and the line rolls without gaps. RESONANCE is right up and ACCENT high, and the accents come in pairs: the accent sweep charges up over a run of accents, so the second of each pair goes higher than the first. The cutoff starts low because the idea is to turn it up as the track builds.

steps.title: Sawtooth, tight and low
steps.why:
A sawtooth with the filter low and a short DECAY, so each of the sixteen notes in a bar stays separate.
- WAVEFORM sawtooth.
- CUT OFF FREQ 2.5 (about 380 Hz), ENV MOD 3, DECAY 2 (about 320 ms).
- Listen for: a fast, muffled rolling pulse with octave jumps.

steps.title: Resonance right up
steps.why:
At full RESONANCE the filter peak is as strong as it goes, so even small filter movement squeals.
- RESONANCE 10.
- Listen for: the line turns from a pulse into a chattering whistle on every note.

steps.title: Accents that build
steps.why:
The size of the accent sweep is ACCENT × (0.6 + 2.6 × RESONANCE/10) octaves, so at these settings it is nearly three octaves. Accents also charge up over a run: two accents in a row push the filter further than one.
- ACCENT 9.
- Listen for: the accented pairs. The second note of each pair shrieks higher than the first.

steps.title: Open it by hand
steps.why:
Records like this are performed on CUT OFF FREQ, opening the filter over many bars. Set a middle point to hear where it is heading.
- CUT OFF FREQ 4 (about 650 Hz).
- Listen for: the whole line gets brighter and harder. Keep turning towards 7 and it starts to scream.

context.filter.cutoff: The performance control here. Start low and turn it up over a minute or more; that slow climb is the build.
context.filter.res: At full, so every note whistles and the accent sweep is as large as it gets.
context.amp.accent: High, and the accents come in pairs so the sweep charges up. Turn it to 3 and the pairs sound like the other notes.
context.env.decay: Short, so sixteen notes a bar stay separate. Turn it up and they blur into one long squelch.
context.filter.envMod: Kept low so the accents stand out against the ordinary notes.

tweaks.try: Sweep from 2 to 7 over about 30 seconds
tweaks.hear: The line climbs from a muffled pulse to a piercing scream.
The whistle goes and the accent pairs shrink, because the accent sweep depends on RESONANCE.
The notes smear together into one rolling squelch.

sounds.name: Dotted Phase
sounds.ref: In the style of Emmanuel Top — "Acid Phase"
sounds.blurb: An acid techno line whose accents fall every three steps, so they drift against the four-to-the-floor beat.
sounds.how: The accents land on steps 1, 4, 7, 10 and 13: groups of three sixteenths played against a beat of four. The pattern of bright notes shifts against the beat while the bar still repeats every sixteen steps. A short DECAY and low ENV MOD keep the ordinary notes dark, so the accents carry the rhythm.

steps.title: Short, dark notes
steps.why:
The ordinary notes are kept dark and short so they sit in the background.
- WAVEFORM sawtooth, CUT OFF FREQ 3.
- ENV MOD 2.5, DECAY 2 (about 320 ms).
- Listen for: an even sixteenth-note pulse with little to mark out the groups.

steps.title: Resonance
steps.why:
RESONANCE gives the notes their acid edge and makes the accent sweep larger.
- RESONANCE 8.
- Listen for: a little squelch on each note.

steps.title: Accents in threes
steps.why:
With ACCENT turned up, the accents every three steps become the rhythm you hear first.
- ACCENT 8.
- Listen for: count four beats while the riff plays. The bright notes land on the beat, then just after it, then before it, and so on round the bar.

context.amp.accent: Carries the three-step rhythm. At 0 the line is an even pulse and the cross-rhythm disappears.
context.filter.envMod: Low, so only the accents open the filter much.
context.env.decay: Short, so each accent is a clear hit.
context.filter.res: Sets the squelch and how far each accent sweeps.

tweaks.hear: The three-step rhythm comes and goes while the notes stay the same.
Every note opens, so the accents no longer stand out and the cross-rhythm blurs.

sounds.name: Funk Stab Line
sounds.ref: In the style of Daft Punk — "Da Funk"
sounds.blurb: A slower, funky line with gaps, off-beat notes and a held note that bends into the next.
sounds.how: The rests matter as much as the notes: they leave space for the beat, and the off-beat notes give the swing. Resonance is moderate, so the notes have a rubbery bite without a full acid squeal. A slide into a tied note at the end of the second bar bends the pitch down without restarting the envelopes.

steps.title: Sawtooth, middle filter
steps.why:
A sawtooth with the filter half open, so the notes are bright enough to carry a melody.
- WAVEFORM sawtooth.
- CUT OFF FREQ 4 (about 650 Hz).
- Listen for: the shape of the riff, with its gaps and off-beat notes.

steps.title: Rubbery, not squealing
steps.why:
Moderate RESONANCE and ENV MOD give each note a bite at the front without the full acid sound.
- RESONANCE 6, ENV MOD 5.
- DECAY 3 (about 400 ms): short enough to keep the gaps clean.
- Listen for: a "dow" at the start of each note.

steps.title: Accents on the jumps
steps.why:
The octave jumps, the low F and one D are accented, so they hit hardest.
- ACCENT 7.
- Listen for: the jump up to the high G on step 4 is louder and brighter. Near the end of the second bar, A sharp slides into G, which is held over two steps.

context.filter.res: Moderate, for bite without squeal. Above 8 it turns into an acid line.
context.filter.envMod: Gives each note its "dow". At 0 the notes are flat.
context.env.decay: Short, so the rests stay clear.
context.amp.accent: Makes the octave jumps hit hard.

tweaks.hear: The line starts to squelch and sounds more like acid house than funk.
A hollower, softer line, closer to a plain synth bass.
Notes ring into the gaps and the groove loses its snap.

sounds.name: Hollow Square Line
sounds.ref: In the style of late-1980s UK acid house
sounds.blurb: An acid line on the square wave, rounder and more hollow than the sawtooth, tuned down to A.
sounds.how: The square wave has only odd harmonics, so with the same resonance it squelches with a hollow, woody tone instead of a buzz. The riff is written in C, and TUNING moves the whole instrument down three semitones so it plays in A. Everything else is the usual acid set-up of resonance, envelope and accents.

steps.title: Square wave
steps.why:
The WAVEFORM switch on the back edge picks the square wave.
- WAVEFORM square.
- Listen for: a hollow tone. Switch to sawtooth and back to compare.

steps.title: Tune down to A
steps.why:
TUNING shifts every note by the same amount, so a riff written in C can be moved to match a track in another key.
- TUNING −3: three semitones down, from C to A.
- Listen for: the whole riff drops in pitch with its shape unchanged.

steps.title: Acid filter settings
steps.why:
The usual acid filter: low cutoff, high resonance, and a medium envelope.
- CUT OFF FREQ 4, RESONANCE 8, ENV MOD 5.
- DECAY 4 (about 500 ms).
- Listen for: a squelch on each note, softer and rounder than on the sawtooth.

steps.title: Accents
steps.why:
The accents on steps 4 and 12 mark the bar.
- ACCENT 6.
- Listen for: those two notes are louder and close quickly.

context.osc.wave: The square wave is what makes this line hollow. The sawtooth is brighter and buzzier.
context.osc.tuning: Moves the riff from C to A. Each whole number is one semitone.
context.filter.res: High, for the squelch. On the square wave it sounds rounder than on the sawtooth.
context.filter.cutoff: The square has less top end, so the cutoff sits a little higher than for a sawtooth line.

tweaks.hear: The riff plays in C, then in D.
The hollow, reedy character of the square wave comes through clearly.

sounds.name: Raga Line
sounds.ref: In the style of Charanjit Singh — "Ten Ragas to a Disco Beat"
sounds.blurb: A melody an octave above the usual bass range, using a raga-like scale with a flattened second and sixth.
sounds.how: The notes come from a scale with D flat and A flat in place of D and A, which gives the line its Indian sound. Played an octave higher than a bass line, the TB-303 becomes a lead. A moderate cutoff and resonance keep the melody clear, and slides give it a sung quality.

steps.title: Sawtooth in the lead range
steps.why:
The riff sits an octave above the other sounds, up to middle C. Higher notes need a higher cutoff, or the filter dulls them.
- WAVEFORM sawtooth.
- CUT OFF FREQ 5 (about 900 Hz).
- Listen for: a melody rather than a bass line.

steps.title: Clear, singing filter
steps.why:
Enough resonance to give the notes a voice, but not so much that the melody turns into squelch.
- RESONANCE 6, ENV MOD 4.
- DECAY 4 (about 500 ms).
- Listen for: each note has a soft "wah" and the pitches stay easy to follow.

steps.title: Accents
steps.why:
The accents mark the top of each phrase.
- ACCENT 6.
- Listen for: the upper C on step 3 rings out, and on steps 5 and 6 B slides up into C.

context.filter.cutoff: Higher than for a bass line, so the upper notes are not muffled.
context.filter.res: Moderate, so the melody stays clear. Above 8 it turns into squelch.
context.filter.envMod: A soft opening on each note.
context.amp.accent: How much the accented top notes of each phrase stand out.

tweaks.hear: The melody squeals and becomes an acid lead.
The whole melody moves down a fourth, to G.

sounds.name: Dub Drift
sounds.ref: In the style of slow dub and ambient acid
sounds.blurb: A slow line of long, tied notes that open and close at walking pace.
sounds.how: At 92 BPM with ties holding each note for three steps, there is time to hear the whole filter sweep. DECAY is near the top, about 1.6 seconds, so the filter closes slowly through each note. The volume envelope has no panel control and cuts off when a note ends, so the ties are what make the notes long.

steps.title: Dark sawtooth
steps.why:
A sawtooth with the filter low, so the notes are deep and round at rest.
- WAVEFORM sawtooth.
- CUT OFF FREQ 2.5 (about 380 Hz).
- Listen for: long, dark notes with plenty of space between them.

steps.title: Long decay
steps.why:
DECAY sets how long the filter takes to close. Near the top it lasts longer than the notes themselves.
- DECAY 9 (about 1.6 s).
- ENV MOD 6: a wide opening on each note.
- Listen for: each note starts bright and dims slowly while it is held.

steps.title: Resonance
steps.why:
RESONANCE turns the slow close into a slow "wow".
- RESONANCE 8.
- Listen for: a vowel-like sweep through each held note. The slid notes bend up into C without starting the sweep again.

steps.title: Soft accents
steps.why:
Accented steps close the filter in 0.2 s whatever DECAY says, which would cut across the slow sweeps. ACCENT is kept low.
- ACCENT 3.
- Listen for: the accented F near the end is only a little louder and closes faster than the other notes.

context.env.decay: Near the top, so the filter closes slowly through each held note. Below 5 the notes go dark almost at once.
context.filter.envMod: How far each note opens before the slow close.
context.filter.res: Makes the slow close a vowel-like "wow".
context.amp.accent: Low, because accents shorten the filter close to 0.2 s and break up the slow sweeps.

tweaks.hear: From short dark notes to long sweeps that are still closing when the next note comes.
The notes stay bright all the way through and the space between them fills up.

sounds.name: Accent Blips
sounds.ref: In the style of early electro
sounds.blurb: Short, high blips with every note accented, used as a percussive part rather than a bass.
sounds.how: The notes are short and high, with the filter closed and ENV MOD near the top, so each one is a quick bright click that dies away. Lighting the ACCENT button accents every note, which makes the filter close in 0.2 s and adds the accent sweep to each one. The result works like a tuned percussion part.

steps.title: Closed filter, big envelope
steps.why:
With the filter almost closed and ENV MOD high, each note is a short burst of brightness on a dark background.
- WAVEFORM sawtooth, CUT OFF FREQ 1.5.
- ENV MOD 9: a large opening. It also lowers the resting cutoff, so between blips there is almost nothing.
- DECAY 0 (about 200 ms): the shortest close.
- Listen for: short, high clicks spaced across the bar.

steps.title: Some resonance
steps.why:
RESONANCE gives each blip a pitched ring as the filter closes.
- RESONANCE 6.
- Listen for: a "pew" on each note instead of a plain click.

steps.title: Accent every note
steps.why:
Lit, the ACCENT button accents every note played, whatever the riff says. With the ACCENT knob up, each blip is louder and gets the accent sweep.
- ACCENT button on.
- ACCENT 7.
- Listen for: the blips are sharper and louder. Turn the ACCENT button off to hear the plain version.

context.filter.envMod: Near the top, so each note is a quick bright burst from a closed filter.
context.env.decay: At 0 for the shortest blip. Raise it and the blips turn into plucks.
context.seq.accent: Lit, so every note is accented: louder, with a 0.2 s filter close and the accent sweep.
context.amp.accent: How much the ACCENT button adds to each blip.
context.filter.res: Gives the blips their pitched "pew".

tweaks.hear: The blips are quieter and less sharp, because they are no longer accented.
Each blip rings with a high whistle.
The blips become longer plucks with a "wah".

sounds.name: Slow Broken Chord
sounds.ref: In the style of ambient electronica
sounds.blurb: A slow arpeggio that climbs up through an A minor chord and back down, then does the same over F.
sounds.how: Each note of the chord is tied over two steps, so the line moves in eighth notes at a relaxed 84 BPM. RESONANCE is low and DECAY long, so the filter only brightens each note a little and closes slowly, which keeps the sound soft. Two slides join the top of each chord to the next note down without restarting the envelopes.

steps.title: Sawtooth, filter half closed
steps.why:
A sawtooth through a filter set fairly low, so the arpeggio is warm rather than buzzy.
- WAVEFORM sawtooth.
- CUT OFF FREQ 4 (about 650 Hz).
- Listen for: the broken chord going up and down. The notes are evenly spaced eighth notes.

steps.title: Low resonance, small sweep
steps.why:
Without much resonance the filter shapes the tone and does not squelch.
- RESONANCE 2: almost no peak.
- ENV MOD 3: each note gets only a little brighter at the start.
- Listen for: soft, even notes with no "yow".

steps.title: Long decay, quiet accents
steps.why:
A long DECAY lets the filter close slowly through each tied note. The riff has no accents, so ACCENT is turned down in case you light the ACCENT button.
- DECAY 8 (about 1.3 s).
- ACCENT 2.
- Listen for: the long C at the top of each chord. It dims slowly as it is held, then slides down to the next note.

context.env.decay: Long, so each note fades in brightness gently. Below 4 the notes become short plucks.
context.filter.res: Kept low so the arpeggio stays soft. Above about 6 it starts to squelch.
context.filter.envMod: Small, so each note brightens only a little at the start.
context.filter.cutoff: Sets how warm the whole line is. Above 6 it gets thin and buzzy.

tweaks.hear: The arpeggio moves from muffled to bright without changing its rhythm.
A hollower, rounder arpeggio, closer to a soft organ.

sounds.name: Pulse Under a Pad
sounds.ref: In the style of ambient and downtempo pulse bass lines
sounds.blurb: A soft square-wave bass playing steady eighth notes, meant to sit under a slow pad.
sounds.how: The square wave and a low filter with almost no resonance give a round, quiet note. Each note is the same length and the same strength, so the line works as a steady pulse rather than a tune. The pitch moves only once, from D to A and back, so a pad played over it has room to change chords.

steps.title: Square wave
steps.why:
The square wave has only odd harmonics, so it is hollow and round.
- WAVEFORM square.
- Listen for: a steady pulse of eighth notes, D for one bar and A for the next.

steps.title: Low, gentle filter
steps.why:
The filter is low with little resonance and a small sweep, so each note has a soft start and no squelch.
- CUT OFF FREQ 3 (about 450 Hz).
- RESONANCE 1.
- ENV MOD 2.
- Listen for: a round, muted pulse that does not draw attention.

steps.title: Medium decay, no accent
steps.why:
DECAY is set so the filter is still closing as each note ends, which smooths the start of every note. ACCENT is off so every note is the same.
- DECAY 5 (about 630 ms).
- ACCENT 0.
- Listen for: no note stands out from the others.

context.osc.wave: The square is what keeps the pulse round. The sawtooth is brighter and fights with a pad.
context.filter.cutoff: Low, so the pulse sits under other parts. Raise it if the pulse gets lost in a mix.
context.filter.res: Almost off, so the notes do not squelch.
context.filter.envMod: Small, for a soft start to each note.
context.env.decay: Middle setting. Shorter gives a clipped pulse; longer gives a smoother one.
context.amp.accent: Off, so every note is the same strength.

tweaks.hear: Each note starts with a clear thump and the pulse becomes more rhythmic.
The whole line moves up a tone, from D to E, to fit a different key.

sounds.name: Chill-Out Glide
sounds.ref: In the style of early-1990s ambient house
sounds.blurb: A slow melody in the middle register where most notes glide into the next.
sounds.how: The notes overlap, so the TB-303 slides between them and does not restart its envelopes. A long DECAY and some resonance make the filter close slowly through each phrase, and with the volume envelope also running on, a slid phrase gets gradually softer. The square wave and a moderate cutoff keep the tone smooth.

steps.title: Square wave, middle register
steps.why:
The melody sits an octave or so above a bass line, so it is played as a lead. The square wave is softer than the sawtooth up here.
- WAVEFORM square.

sounds.how: City pop bass is busy and glossy, full of octave pops and syncopation over lush chords. A brighter saw with a quick pluck pops like a slapped string.
